schemes.description: Central Careers (Career Lab) extracurricular programme. After initial training, final-year undergraduates and taught postgraduates are placed in small multidisciplinary teams matched to an external organisation (charity/NGO, startup or large corporate) and work on that organisation's real challenge for four weeks (three for the summer run, c.20 hours in total), ending with a team presentation of recommendations to the client. Students receive a Real Living Wage-linked bursary paid by the university.

schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Final-year undergraduates and taught postgraduates (no school restriction stated)
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Final-year UG and taught PG only; one participation per academic year; application required. PGT on courses with a guaranteed work project receive separate communication.
schemes.credit_assessment: Non-credit; paid bursary (GBP 269 for Winter 2025 / Spring 2026 runs)
schemes.duration: 3-4 weeks (c.20 hours) after training; three runs a year (winter, spring, summer)
schemes.delivery_format: Mostly remote research; team presentation to client
schemes.project_evidence: Teams address a real organisational challenge/brief and present recommendations to the client [1][2][3].
schemes.group_evidence: Students placed in small multidisciplinary teams; a five-student team worked on the Hastings Direct brief [1][3].
schemes.employer_evidence: External organisations set the project briefs and receive the team's presentation; e.g. Hastings Direct set a brief on its SDG contributions and later made changes partly aligned to the recommendations [1][3][4].
schemes.partner_role: Sets brief (client) and receives final presentation; organisations pay nothing (university funds student bursary).
schemes.named_partners: Hastings Direct (2024 case study); AECOM, Komedia, Mindlab (past clients, undated page)
schemes.deliverable: Team presentation of recommendations to client
schemes.unresolved: Exact eligibility wording (whether all schools/IDS/BSMS included) not quoted; 2023 organisations guide describes an older 100-hour Riipen-based format. Relationship to the 'Changing the Face of Consultancy' variant (broadcast 66181) not tested.

profile_md:
**Reduced-depth review; all six areas queried.**

- **Central:** The **Career Lab Student Consultancy Programme** qualifies. Final-year undergraduates and taught postgraduates apply; selected students form small multidisciplinary teams that spend 3-4 weeks (c.20 hours) working on a brief set by an external organisation (charities/NGOs, startups, large corporates such as Hastings Direct) and present recommendations to the client. It is extracurricular, bursary-paid and runs three times in 2026/27.
- **Business School:** The PG **Consultancy Project (111N1)** is a 30-credit summer group live consultancy for local organisations/businesses (e.g. Management MSc dissertation alternative), but the latest dated evidence is 2024/25. The UG **Marketing Consultancy Project (Capstone)** is a team brief-based capstone current in 2026 but with no evidenced real client (only tips from a consulting firm).
- The legacy **Connector Programme** is an internal student-staff partnership scheme and does not meet criterion C.

Engineering (MEng Group Project, no external client evidenced), sciences, arts/social sciences, Law Clinics and BSMS/IDS yielded no verified qualifying scheme at this depth; the Career Lab programme is promoted on Physics and Media MSc pages as paid project opportunities.
gaps: Reduced-depth: one query per area. PG Consultancy Project (S3) lacks 2025/26+ corroboration and client sector. Marketing capstone client unknown. Law Clinics, Community Media, Chemistry Industrial Project, Business Analytics/IBD projects, Changing the Face of Consultancy untested; further departmental instances likely.
